title: Inference tabletop recovery battlecard - seller ops quickrun
content:
Purpose / one-liner:
Quick, rehearsable seller + ops tabletop to demonstrate Redwood’s resiliency story in a 30–45 minute customer-runthrough. Focus: tangible recovery levers, customer questions, scripts for sellers, and the artifacts ops will show in a live demo.

When to use this:
- During late-stage pilots where reliability & incident response are the remaining risks
- Executive Q&A with platform/infra stakeholders (SRE, platform eng)
- Renewal or procurement meetings where SLAs and runbooks are negotiated

Session outline (30–45 min):
1) 5 min – framing: why we do tabletop (scope, anchors, non-goals)
2) 10 min – scenario walkthrough #1 (regional GPU/egress outage) + live dashboard walkthrough
3) 10 min – scenario walkthrough #2 (model-quality regression / hallucinations) + rollback / canary demo
4) 5–10 min – Q&A + negotiation triggers (SLA language, escalation commitments)
5) 5 min – close: next steps and artifacts to leave behind

Prep checklist (seller & ops):
- Seller: confirm attendee list includes SRE/platform contact (name, email) and procurement lead
- Ops: ensure Console demo workspace has a canned incident (non-prod) and screenshots pre-captured (traces, per-route latency, token cost breakdown)
- Joint: share a one-pager 24h before with scenario bullets and expected roles

Scenario A – Regional outage (the classic “single region GPU cloud failure”):
- Trigger: Major public cloud region has a zone failure; capacity drops 60% for 10–30 minutes. Customer sees elevated tail latency and partial 5xx errors.
- Seller story: emphasize routing policy, multi-region fallback, reserved capacity, and graceful degradation.
- Ops actions to demo:
  - Show Console routing policy UI and the active fallback (route to dedicated pool in another region)
  - Show trace that demonstrates failover latency delta (10–100ms depending on variant)
  - Toggle simulated capacity pressure -> show automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (smaller quantized model)
- Scripted seller lines: "We design for graceful degradation — you keep throughput and lower cost predictability by failing to a verified variant, not to an unknown model."
- Typical customer pushback: "Can we trust the smaller model quality?" 
  - Quick answer: show pre-run BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity snapshots for representative prompts and highlight rollback options.

Scenario B – Model-quality regression (hallucination spike):
- Trigger: New model rollout introduced a prompt-dependant hallucination behavior; customer noticed a spike in bad outputs in production.
- Seller story: highlight canary rollouts, per-prompt evals, and automatic regression alerts tied to prompt-sets (Redwood Optimize).
- Ops actions to demo:
  - Show per-prompt quality dashboard and the alert triggered by the eval set (sample diffs + score drop)
  - Demonstrate automated rollback (canary -> previous pinned model) and how traffic is shifted (5%->0% over N minutes)
  - Show integrated evidence (example inputs/outputs) that you can hand back to the engineering team
- Scripted seller lines: "We surface regressions before they scale: your canary runs against your golden prompts and we keep the last-good model pinned for instant rollback."
- Negotiation hooks: keep a copy of the prompt/eval set as part of the contract appendix for auditability.

Scenario C – KV cache / persistent KV outage causing latency spike:
- Trigger: Cache layer is unreachable, increasing per-request inference work and token cost.
- Seller story: explain prefix caching, cache warmup, and how Redwood’s routing prioritizes low-latency paths during cache misses.
- Ops actions to demo:
  - Show cache miss rate and token cost step-change in Console billing view
  - Show recommended mitigation: ephemeral pre-warm, adjust batching for throughput, or shift to reserved nodes with cache pinning
- Scripted seller defense: "We can quantify the unit-cost delta and run a temporary reserved capacity for the spike window — we’ll coordinate a cost share if it’s a platform fault."

Roles & escalation commitments (what to promise live):
- Ops will show: live Console, canary rollback, and routing policy change in <5 minutes (prep these beforehand).
- Seller will own: customer communication script, follow-up ticket, and SLA negotiation notes.
- Escalation matrix example to offer customer (keep short):
  1) Customer-facing SE (within 15m during office hours)
  2) On-call SRE (30–60m acknowledge)
  3) Eng incident lead (2–4 hours for full incident report)

Artifacts to leave behind (deliverable bundle):
- 1-page tabletop summary (scenario + outcome + artifacts shown)
- Console snapshots: route histogram, token cost delta graph, canary traffic timeline, alert log sample
- Action items doc with owner and SLA language draft for procurement
- Example contract appendix: pinned-eval-sets and rollback SLAs (editable)

Fast rebuttals cheat-sheet (short):
- "We’ll just stop using you" -> Lead with multi-tier fallback: regional + quantized variants + reserved capacity; show cost/latency tradeoff numbers immediately.
- "How do we audit quality?" -> Offer prompt-set snapshots, automated eval logs (immutable), and periodic quality reviews.
- "What about data exfil?" -> Talk about Private deployments, VPC control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs.

Metrics you should show (one-slide snapshots):
- Per-route 95/99 latency pre/post-failover
- Token cost per 1k requests (before and during fallback)
- Canary failure rate and triggered rollback timestamp
- Time-to-first-response for SE/SRE during the tabletop (measured to prove SLA)

Follow-up play (post-session):
1) Email bundle with artifacts + editable contract appendix (seller)
2) Ops.schedule: 1-week follow-up runbook walk-through with customer SREs
3) If the customer requests, run a joint DR test in their non-prod region (scope/cost)

Open questions / things to refine: (notes to self)
- Need a concise pre-canned demo dataset for hallucination scenario (legal/PII-safe)
- Make Console screenshots generic (no customer data) but believable (timestamps, heatmap spikes)
- Get buy-in from infra on promised timing for live toggles (don’t promise <5m if it’s longer)

Appendix: quick seller scripts (30 sec vignettes)
- Exec opener (30s): "We’ll run two short failure scenarios to show how Redwood preserves availability and quality—first, a region outage where we fail traffic to a verified variant and reserved pool. Second, a model-quality regression where we show the canary and automated rollback. The goal is to leave you with a playbook and artifact bundle you can take to procurement."
- Platform question (SRE): "What’s the RTO for a canary rollback?" -> "We aim for automated rollback to be triggered within monitoring thresholds; in our demo we’ll show a 10–15 minute recovery window from alert to <1% impacted traffic. For enterprise contracts we’ll pin a lower RTO in the SLA."
- Procurement push: "We need indemnities for model drift." -> "We include pinned-eval appendix and a routine review cadence; we’ll put formal rollback and audit commitments in the contract appendix."

End — lightweight, modular tabletop that sellers can run with Ops co-present. Keep this doc as the canonical quickrun; link full runbook from Confluence (INF-TRG-221) and attach editable appendix before each run.
